newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 11.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- Insurance and financial company Aetna Inc will reduce its work force by 4,400 jobs or 13 percent.
- Monsanto Co plans to sell or spin off its chemical operations in order to concentrate on its drug biotechnology lines and popular products like Nutrasweet and Roundup.
- Ford Motor Co named Jacques Nasser to lead its North American and European automotive operations.
- U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation arrested 36 people for securities fraud and conspiracy to commit securities fraud in a sting operation.
- U.S. retailers reported mixed same-store sales for September.
- Olin Corp said it planned to spin off its aerospace and ordnance operations, sell its isocyanate chemical business and buy back 10 percent of its stock.
- General Electric reported third-quarter earnings of $1.08 per share, a 13-percent increase over the same period last year.
- True North Communications Inc will combine its TN Technologies unit with Modem Media Advertizing in a $29 million stock deal.
- Connecticut's Northeast Utilities said it would likely not restart the Connecticut Yankee nuclear power plant in Haddam Neck due to high costs.
- Shareholders of Time Warner Inc and Turner Broadcasting System Inc approved the $7 billion merger of the two companies.
- The Dow Jones industrial average lost 8.95 to close at 5,921.67 as the market remained cautious towards quarterly earnings reported and September inflation.
- U.S. treasury prices also fell amid worries about inflation and interest rates.
